business.what_it_does: Buffer is social media management software for small businesses to create and schedule posts, analyze results, and engage with their community across connected social channels.
business.business_model: Self-serve subscription software with a free plan and paid plans priced per connected channel, billed monthly or yearly.

facts.statement: Buffer is made for small businesses and provides tools to schedule posts, analyze results, and engage with their community.

provenance.source: What is Buffer and where can I watch a demo?
provenance.quote: Buffer is a social media management software made for small businesses, providing the tools they need to schedule posts, analyze the results, and engage with their community.

facts.statement: Users can publish through Buffer's web application, mobile app, or browser extension.

provenance.source: What is Buffer and where can I watch a demo?
provenance.quote: You can publish posts through our web application at buffer.com, through our mobile app, or through the browser extension.

facts.statement: Buffer supports publishing to Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest, TikTok, Google Business Profiles, Start Pages, Mastodon, YouTube Shorts, Threads, Bluesky, and Substack, with analytics and engagement availability varying by channel type.

facts.statement: Insights provides single-channel and cross-channel views of follower growth, engagement, and impressions inside the publishing dashboard.

provenance.quote: It's a lightweight analytics view built right into Buffer — check in on a single channel's follower growth, engagement, and impressions, or get a cross-channel overview of how all your channels are performing, all without ever leaving your publishing dashboard.

facts.statement: Insights includes period comparisons, a sortable Performance per Post table, follower growth charts, tag filters, and AI-powered Takeaways.

provenance.source: What is Buffer and where can I watch a demo?
provenance.quote: Features include summary metrics compared against an earlier period, a Performance per Post table you can sort to find your best content, follower growth charts, tag filters for tracking campaigns, and AI-powered Takeaways that suggest what to post next.

facts.statement: Paid plans can export Insights as CSV, Markdown, or branded PDF reports; chart snapshots are downloadable on every plan, including Free.

provenance.source: What is Buffer and where can I watch a demo?
provenance.quote: On our paid plans, you can also export your Insights as a CSV, Markdown, or branded PDF report. Chart snapshots can be downloaded on every plan, including Free.

facts.statement: Buffer has a comment inbox for replying to Instagram comments.

provenance.source: What is Buffer and where can I watch a demo?
provenance.quote: We’ve created a comment inbox feature that helps you turn every Instagram comment into a meaningful interaction. Features include a grid of all your Instagram posts and allowing you to effortlessly reply to each comment.

facts.statement: Queue posts can be reordered by drag and drop, moved to the top, moved to the next available slot, or shuffled.

provenance.quote: You can do this by dragging and dropping posts into the desired order, or if you feel like really shaking things up, you can use the Shuffle feature to mix up the order of the first 200 posts in your queue.

facts.statement: The Shuffle feature changes the order of the first 200 eligible posts in a queue.

provenance.quote: The Shuffle feature allows you to mix up the order of the first 200 posts in your queue.

facts.statement: Custom scheduled posts are locked in place and cannot be moved using drag and drop, Move to Top, or Move to Next Available Slot.

provenance.quote: It is not possible to move custom scheduled posts using Move to Top or Move to Next Available Slot, since custom scheduled posts are locked in place.

facts.statement: Queue reordering requires selecting a specific channel rather than All Channels.

provenance.quote: You can't move posts while All Channels is selected. Instead, please choose a specific channel from the left side before attempting to reorder your posts.

facts.statement: The Free plan permits up to three simultaneous channel connections and has a lifetime limit of eight unique channel connections per social network.

provenance.quote: While our Free plan supports connections for up to three channels at once, there is a lifetime channel connection limit of 8 channels per social network.

facts.statement: Google Business Profiles are not supported in Insights because of API limitations.

provenance.quote: Google Business Profiles are not supported in Insights due to API limitations.

entries.verbatim: - **Export as PDF** — opens a short configuration step first, where you can set a custom report name, upload a cover logo, and choose which sections to include (see [Customizing your PDF export](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/using-insights-in-buffer-x4gLauQU5a#h-customizing-your-pdf-export) below). Buffer then generates a branded PDF report of your current Insights view.

entries.claim: An All Channels PDF export includes an aggregated Summary, Top 5 Posts by Reactions, Top 5 Posts by Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and a detailed section for each channel.
entries.verbatim: - For the All Channels view, the export includes an aggregated Summary, Top 5 Posts by Reactions, Top 5 Posts by Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and a detailed section for each channel with its own Summary metrics, charts, and top posts.

entries.claim: Each channel’s detailed section in an All Channels PDF includes Summary metrics, charts, and top posts.
entries.verbatim: - For the All Channels view, the export includes an aggregated Summary, Top 5 Posts by Reactions, Top 5 Posts by Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and a detailed section for each channel with its own Summary metrics, charts, and top posts.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots downloads all Insights charts as images.
entries.verbatim: - **Download Snapshots** — downloads all of your Insights charts as images for easy sharing

entries.claim: Insights exports are generated in the background, and the tab must remain open until the download begins.
entries.verbatim: 5. The file will generate in the background. Smaller exports download almost immediately; larger ones (long date ranges or high post counts) may take a few minutes. A spinner will show while the file is being prepared so keep the tab open until the download starts.

entries.claim: The PDF report name appears in the PDF header, and Buffer uses the organization name when the field is blank.
entries.verbatim: - **Report name**: a custom title shown in the PDF header. Leave it blank and Buffer will use your organization name instead.

entries.claim: A custom cover logo can replace default Buffer branding on the PDF report cover.
entries.verbatim: - **Cover logo**: upload your own logo to replace the default Buffer branding on the report's cover. Buffer saves the last logo you upload, so you won't need to re-upload it on your next export.

entries.claim: Buffer saves the last uploaded PDF cover logo for the next export.
entries.verbatim: Buffer saves the last logo you upload, so you won't need to re-upload it on your next export.

entries.claim: Every PDF section is included by default and can be unchecked before export.
entries.verbatim: - **Sections to include**: every section is on by default. Uncheck anything you don't want in the final PDF.

entries.claim: The export configuration step applies only to PDF exports; CSV and Markdown exports start immediately.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** This configuration step only applies to PDF exports. CSV and Markdown exports run immediately, with no extra step.

entries.claim: Buffer Insights exports a Summary containing each metric’s current value and percentage change versus the previous period.
entries.verbatim: - **Summary** — each metric's current value and its percentage change vs. the previous period.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post export provides one row per post.
entries.verbatim: - **Performance per Post** — one row per post, including Post ID, published date and time, a post excerpt, post type (image, reel, carousel, video, etc.), post URL, any Buffer tags applied, and all available metrics for that channel (impressions, reach, reactions, comments, shares, saves, engagement rate, and so on). Only metrics that exist for the channel are included.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post export includes the Post ID, published date and time, a post excerpt, post type, post URL, and applied Buffer tags.
entries.verbatim: - **Performance per Post** — one row per post, including Post ID, published date and time, a post excerpt, post type (image, reel, carousel, video, etc.), post URL, any Buffer tags applied, and all available metrics for that channel (impressions, reach, reactions, comments, shares, saves, engagement rate, and so on). Only metrics that exist for the channel are included.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post export includes all metrics available for the channel, such as impressions, reach, reactions, comments, shares, saves, and engagement rate.
entries.verbatim: - **Performance per Post** — one row per post, including Post ID, published date and time, a post excerpt, post type (image, reel, carousel, video, etc.), post URL, any Buffer tags applied, and all available metrics for that channel (impressions, reach, reactions, comments, shares, saves, engagement rate, and so on). Only metrics that exist for the channel are included.

entries.claim: The Metrics Over Time export includes daily followers, posts published, and post views for the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - **Metrics Over Time** — daily followers, posts published, and post views for the selected period.

entries.claim: Insights exports omit empty metric columns and include only metrics reported by the channel.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** Metrics included in the export vary by channel, just as they do in the Insights dashboard. You won't see empty columns — only the metrics your channel actually reports.

entries.claim: Each Insights export exactly reflects the filters active at the time of export.
entries.verbatim: **Tip:** If you want a different slice of your data, just update your filters and export again. Each export reflects the current state of your filters exactly.

entries.claim: The Summary compares channel performance during a selected date range with another chosen period.
entries.verbatim: The Summary section gives you a snapshot of how your channel performed during the selected date range, compared to another period of your choice.

entries.claim: The default Previous Period comparison uses the same number of days immediately before the selected range.
entries.verbatim: - **Previous Period** — the same number of days immediately before your selected range (default).

entries.claim: Same Period Last Week compares with the equivalent calendar window one week earlier and is unavailable for selected ranges longer than 7 days.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Week** — the equivalent calendar window one week earlier. Best for short-range, week-over-week check-ins. (Unavailable when your selected date range is longer than 7 days.)

entries.claim: Same Period Last Month compares with the same calendar dates one month earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Month** — the same calendar dates one month back.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Year compares with the same calendar dates one year earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Year** — the same calendar dates one year back.

entries.claim: A Custom comparison uses a historical start date and a comparison window equal in length to the current period.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, can't be selected.

entries.claim: Custom comparison dates cannot overlap the current period or be in the future.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, can't be selected.

entries.claim: Each Summary metric updates its comparison indicator to reflect the selected comparison period.
entries.verbatim: Each metric updates its comparison indicator (e.g. ↑ 28.6%) to reflect the period you've selected.

entries.claim: The Compare to dropdown is available only on single-channel Insights pages, not the All Channels view.
entries.verbatim: - The **Compare to** dropdown is currently available on single-channel Insights pages only. It does not appear on the All Channels view.

entries.claim: Bookmarked Insights views save both the comparison choice and date range and restore both when reopened.
entries.verbatim: - Your comparison choice is now saved alongside the date range when you bookmark a view, so reopening a saved view restores both.

entries.claim: The Followers table shows current followers and the exact number gained or lost during the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Followers table sits right at the top, showing your current followers and exactly how many you've gained (or lost) over your selected date range. We show that as a plain number, like +42, not a percentage, so you can see the real movement at a glance.

entries.claim: Follower movement is displayed as a plain number, such as +42, rather than a percentage.
entries.verbatim: The Followers table sits right at the top, showing your current followers and exactly how many you've gained (or lost) over your selected date range. We show that as a plain number, like +42, not a percentage, so you can see the real movement at a glance.

entries.claim: For networks that do not check follower counts daily, Buffer shows the most recent reading available for the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - Some networks only check in on your follower count every so often instead of daily. When that's the case, you'll see the most recent reading available for your selected period.

entries.claim: The Followers table is hidden when a channel does not report follower data.
entries.verbatim: - If a channel doesn't report follower data at all, the Followers table will be hidden.

entries.claim: The Posts metric counts posts published during the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Posts** — the number of posts published during the period

entries.claim: The Reactions metric totals likes and reactions received across all posts.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** — total likes/reactions received across all posts

entries.claim: The Comments metric totals comments received.
entries.verbatim: - **Comments** — total comments received

entries.claim: The Impressions metric counts the total number of times posts were displayed.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** — total number of times your posts were displayed. For Instagram, this metric is now labeled **Views** everywhere in Insights — on the single-channel page, the All Channels summary, and any mixed-channel selection that includes Instagram — matching what you see on Instagram's own Insights page.

entries.claim: For Instagram, the Impressions metric is labeled Views on the single-channel page, All Channels summary, and mixed-channel selections that include Instagram.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** — total number of times your posts were displayed. For Instagram, this metric is now labeled **Views** everywhere in Insights — on the single-channel page, the All Channels summary, and any mixed-channel selection that includes Instagram — matching what you see on Instagram's own Insights page.

entries.claim: The Shares metric totals shares.
entries.verbatim: - **Shares** — total shares

entries.claim: The Saves metric totals saves.
entries.verbatim: - **Saves** — total saves

entries.claim: The Follows metric counts new followers gained during the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Follows** — new followers gained during the period

entries.claim: The Reach metric counts unique accounts that saw the content.
entries.verbatim: - **Reach** — the number of unique accounts that saw your content

entries.claim: Engagement Rate is the percentage of people who engaged with posts out of those who saw them.
entries.verbatim: - **Engagement Rate** — the percentage of people who engaged with your posts out of those who saw them

entries.claim: Each available Summary metric includes a comparison indicator, such as ↑ 28.6%.
entries.verbatim: Each metric includes a comparison indicator (e.g. ↑ 28.6%) so you can see at a glance how things have changed.

entries.claim: Metric availability varies by channel according to data shared through each social network’s API.
entries.verbatim: - Not all metrics are available for every channel — it depends on what each social network shares through its API. For example, Saves may only appear for Instagram, and Reach may not be available for all networks.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profiles, Reactions count only reactions on the post itself.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** count only the reactions on the post itself, matching what you'd see on LinkedIn.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profiles, Comments include nested replies beneath top-level comments.
entries.verbatim: - **Comments** include nested replies underneath top-level comments, since LinkedIn's own comment total works the same way.

entries.claim: The LinkedIn Reactions and Comments counting rules described for profiles do not apply identically to LinkedIn Pages because Pages use a different API that does not break down totals the same way.
entries.verbatim: - This applies to LinkedIn profile channels. LinkedIn Pages use a different LinkedIn API that doesn't break totals down the same way.

entries.claim: For Substack, Reactions count likes on a Note and Comments count replies.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** count likes on your Note, and **Comments** count replies.

entries.claim: For Substack, Restacks count how many times someone restacked or reshared a Note.
entries.verbatim: - **Restacks** count how many times someone restacked (reshared) your Note on Substack.

entries.claim: For Substack, Impressions count every Note view and Reach counts unique Note viewers.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** count every time your Note was viewed, and **Reach** counts the unique people who viewed it.

entries.claim: For Substack, Shares count clicks on a Note’s share link rather than restacks.
entries.verbatim: - **Shares** count clicks on your Note's share link, not restacks.

entries.claim: For Substack, Free Subscriptions and Paid Subscriptions count subscribers attributed to each Note by Substack.
entries.verbatim: - **Free Subscriptions** and **Paid Subscriptions** count the subscribers Substack attributes to each Note.

entries.claim: Engagement rate is unavailable for Substack because Substack does not share the data required to calculate it.
entries.verbatim: - Engagement rate isn't available for Substack, because Substack doesn't share the numbers needed to calculate one.

entries.claim: Substack follower counts and publication-level statistics such as total subscribers and open rates are unavailable in Buffer and remain in the Substack dashboard.
entries.verbatim: - Follower counts and publication-level stats (like total subscribers or open rates) aren't available for Substack. Those stay in your Substack dashboard.

entries.claim: A single-channel Insights view can turn Summary statistics into a ready-to-publish post.
entries.verbatim: On a single-channel Insights view, you can turn your Summary stats into a ready-to-publish post.

entries.claim: Share as Post generates a branded 1080×1080 image containing top statistics, the channel avatar, and Buffer branding.
entries.verbatim: 2. This will generate a branded 1080×1080 image showing your top stats (reach, likes, replies, shares, etc.) with your channel's avatar and Buffer branding.

entries.claim: Share as Post opens the Post Composer with the generated image attached, alt text set, and a short caption pre-filled.
entries.verbatim: 3. Open the Post Composer with that image attached, alt text set, and a short caption pre-filled.

entries.claim: A shared Summary post can be edited, assigned to channels, and scheduled or published like another post.
entries.verbatim: 4. Tweak the copy, choose which channels to post to, and schedule or publish like any other post.

entries.claim: Share Summary is available only on single-channel Insights and does not appear in All Channels.
entries.verbatim: - **Share Summary is only available on single-channel Insights.** It doesn't appear on the All Channels view because there's no single channel for the post to default to.

entries.claim: Share Summary images always use a 1080×1080 square layout accepted by Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook without further cropping.
entries.verbatim: - The image always uses a 1080×1080 square layout, which Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook all accept without further cropping.

entries.claim: A Share Summary card displays up to 4 available statistics, selected from reach, likes, replies, and shares-style metrics.
entries.verbatim: - Up to 4 stats are shown on the card, picked from what's available for your channel (reach, likes, replies, shares-style metrics).

entries.claim: Download Snapshots packages the Share-as-Post images for every chart into one ZIP without opening the composer.
entries.verbatim: 💡 **Tip:** Want to grab every chart's Share-as-Post image at once? Use ***Download Snapshots*** from the Export menu — it packages them all into a single ZIP without opening the composer. Available on every plan, including Free.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots is available on every Buffer plan, including Free.
entries.verbatim: 💡 **Tip:** Want to grab every chart's Share-as-Post image at once? Use ***Download Snapshots*** from the Export menu — it packages them all into a single ZIP without opening the composer. Available on every plan, including Free.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post table breaks down each individual post’s performance during the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Performance per Post table breaks down how each individual post did during the selected date range.

entries.claim: For each post, the Performance per Post table shows a thumbnail, content preview, engagement rate, reactions, comments, and views.
entries.verbatim: - **Post** — a thumbnail and preview of the post content - **Eng. Rate** — the engagement rate for that post - **Reactions** — the number of likes/reactions for that post

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Views counts how many times the Story was played.
entries.verbatim: - **Views**: how many times the Story was played.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Reach counts unique accounts that saw the Story.
entries.verbatim: - **Reach**: the number of unique accounts that saw the Story.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Replies counts replies sent to the Story.
entries.verbatim: - **Replies**: replies sent to the Story.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, engagement rate is calculated as Interactions divided by Reach.
entries.verbatim: - **Eng. Rate**: engagement rate (Interactions ÷ Reach).

entries.claim: Users can rearrange Performance per Post columns from the column selector.
entries.verbatim: You can also rearrange the order of columns from the column selector, like this:

entries.claim: Clicking a metric column header sorts the Performance per Post table by that metric, and clicking again switches between descending and ascending order.
entries.verbatim: Click any metric column header in the Performance per Post table to sort by that metric. Click again to switch between descending and ascending order.

entries.claim: Sortable Performance per Post metrics may include engagement rate, reactions, comments, views, impressions, reach, shares, reposts, clicks, saves, follows, quotes, total time watched, and viewers.
entries.verbatim: Sortable metrics may include Eng. **Rate, Reactions, Comments, Views, Impressions, Reach, Shares, Reposts, Clicks, Saves, Follows, Quotes, Total time watched,** and **Viewers.**

entries.claim: Sortable columns vary by network and appear only where the channel reports the relevant metric.
entries.verbatim: Sorting is per network. A column is only sortable where that channel actually reports the metric, so the sortable columns you see will vary by channel (for example, Facebook clicks are sortable on Facebook, and LinkedIn viewers and total time watched are sortable on LinkedIn).

entries.claim: Facebook clicks are sortable on Facebook, while viewers and total time watched are sortable on LinkedIn.
entries.verbatim: A column is only sortable where that channel actually reports the metric, so the sortable columns you see will vary by channel (for example, Facebook clicks are sortable on Facebook, and LinkedIn viewers and total time watched are sortable on LinkedIn).

entries.claim: Instagram Reels do not show a Follows column because Meta reports Follows for Feed posts and Stories but not Reels.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** Some metrics also vary by post type. Instagram Reels, for example, don't show a Follows column, since Meta doesn't report Follows for Reels, only for Feed posts and Stories.

entries.claim: The Metrics section displays a line chart for a metric over the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Metrics section shows a line chart of a metric over your selected date range.

entries.claim: Date and tag filters do not affect the Metrics chart, which always shows full-year data regardless of the date range selected elsewhere.
entries.verbatim: Note that date and tag filters do not apply to this chart — it always shows data for the full year regardless of the date range selected elsewhere in Insights.

entries.claim: A channel’s Metrics chart opens on Content Impact by default, layering posts over follower growth.
entries.verbatim: When you open a channel, the chart opens on **Content Impact** by default, layering your posts on top of your follower growth so you can see how the two track together.

entries.claim: The Metrics chart resets to Content Impact each time the user switches channels.
entries.verbatim: Want a different view? Grab one from the buttons below. The default flips back to Content Impact each time you switch channels.

entries.claim: If a channel has no follower data, its Metrics chart opens on Posts instead of Content Impact.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** No follower data for a channel? The chart opens on **Posts** instead.

entries.claim: The Posts chart view shows how often content was published during the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - **Posts** — how often you published during the selected period.

entries.claim: The Content Impact view displays post volume alongside follower growth.
entries.verbatim: - **Content Impact** — your post volume alongside follower growth, side by side.

entries.claim: The Audience Growth view shows followers over time and net new followers gained.
entries.verbatim: - **Audience Growth** — followers over time, plus net new followers gained.

entries.claim: The Visibility view compares impressions—or Views for Instagram—with follower count.
entries.verbatim: - **Visibility** — impressions (or Views, for Instagram) compared against your follower count.

entries.claim: The Follower Growth Rate view is available only for LinkedIn channels and benchmarks monthly follower growth against similar Buffer accounts.
entries.verbatim: - **Follower Growth Rate** *(LinkedIn channels only)* — your monthly follower growth rate benchmarked against similar Buffer accounts. See the callout below for details.

entries.claim: Custom Metric Sets are available on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: - **+ Custom Metric Set** (available on paid plans) — build your own view by selecting the metrics you want to track together.

entries.claim: A Custom Metric Set lets users select metrics to track together.
entries.verbatim: - **+ Custom Metric Set** (available on paid plans) — build your own view by selecting the metrics you want to track together.

entries.claim: Selecting a curated view button automatically updates the Metrics chart.
entries.verbatim: Selecting a button updates the chart automatically.

entries.claim: The metric dropdown can switch the chart to any individual metric available for the channel.
entries.verbatim: You can also use the **metric dropdown** (e.g. Followers) directly above the chart to switch to any individual metric available for your channel.

entries.claim: The Visibility tab appears only for networks that report views data and is hidden for Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon.
entries.verbatim: - The **Visibility** tab (impressions, or Views for Instagram) is only shown for networks that report views data. It's hidden on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon channels — those networks only report follower counts at the channel level, so there's no views data to display.

entries.claim: Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon report only channel-level follower counts and do not provide views data for the Visibility tab.
entries.verbatim: It's hidden on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon channels — those networks only report follower counts at the channel level, so there's no views data to display.

entries.claim: LinkedIn’s Follower Growth Rate benchmark plots monthly follower growth over time, compares it with the median for similar Buffer accounts, and shows a percentile rank.
entries.verbatim: - The **Follower Growth Rate benchmark** is available on LinkedIn channels only. It plots your monthly follower growth rate over time and compares it against the median for a cohort of similar Buffer accounts, showing you a percentile rank so you can see where you stand relative to comparable pages.

entries.claim: LinkedIn benchmark cohorts match accounts by channel type and approximate follower count.
entries.verbatim: - **What counts as a "similar account"?** The cohort is matched on two things: channel type (pages are compared to pages, profiles to profiles) and approximate follower count. It's scoped to other LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer — not LinkedIn as a whole.

entries.claim: LinkedIn benchmark cohorts include other LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer, not LinkedIn as a whole.
entries.verbatim: It's scoped to other LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer — not LinkedIn as a whole.

entries.claim: By default, the All Channels Metrics chart displays the first 5 channels.
entries.verbatim: By default, in the **All Channels view,** the Metrics chart shows your **first 5 channels**.

entries.claim: When the channel filter is applied, the All Channels Metrics chart draws up to 10 selected channels at a time.
entries.verbatim: Apply the channel filter at the top of the page, and the chart switches to your selected channels, drawing **up to 10** at a time.

entries.claim: When more channels exist than the chart can show, Buffer displays an inline notice stating how many of the total are shown and suggesting filtering by channel.
entries.verbatim: When more channels exist than the chart can show, you'll see an inline notice (*"Showing X of Y channels. Filter by channel to see a different set."*) in the section subheading.

entries.claim: Channels that do not report the selected metric are excluded from the Metrics chart with an explanatory notice.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** Some metrics aren't available for every channel. If a channel you've selected doesn't report the metric you're viewing, for example Pinterest doesn't report followers, you'll see a notice like "Pinterest profiles don't report followers, so they are excluded from this chart," and that channel won't be drawn.

entries.claim: Pinterest profiles do not report followers and are excluded from follower charts.
entries.verbatim: If a channel you've selected doesn't report the metric you're viewing, for example Pinterest doesn't report followers, you'll see a notice like "Pinterest profiles don't report followers, so they are excluded from this chart," and that channel won't be drawn.

entries.claim: The All Channels Metrics area contains two stacked cards: Followers above Posts.
entries.verbatim: The All Channels Metrics area is split into two stacked cards — **Followers** on top and **Posts** below.

entries.claim: The All Channels Followers metric offers By channel, Growth, and Over time views.
entries.verbatim: In the **All Channels** view, the **Followers** metric has its own view toggle so you can choose how to look at follower counts:

entries.claim: The By channel follower view is a ranked bar chart with one bar per channel, sorted by current followers.
entries.verbatim: - **By channel** — a ranked bar chart, one bar per channel, sorted by current followers.

entries.claim: In the By channel view, each bar’s solid base represents the lower of the starting or ending follower count, and a coloured segment represents the period’s change.
entries.verbatim: The solid base shows where you started or ended (whichever is lower), and the coloured segment on top shows the change for the period.

entries.claim: In the By channel view, the label above each bar displays current followers and the change in brackets, such as 12,340 (+128).
entries.verbatim: The label at the top of the bar shows current followers and the change in brackets (e.g. "12,340 (+128)").

entries.claim: The Growth follower view is a diverging bar chart of net change per channel, sorted with gains first.
entries.verbatim: - **Growth** — a diverging bar chart of net change per channel, sorted gains-first.

entries.claim: In the Growth view, gains are green and losses are red.
entries.verbatim: Bars are coloured by direction — green for gains, red for losses — so you can spot at a glance which channels grew and which shrank.

entries.claim: The Growth view omits the channel-colour legend because colour indicates direction.
entries.verbatim: The channel-colour legend isn't shown in this view because colour is being used to mean direction here.

entries.claim: The Over time follower view is a line or area chart of followers across the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Over time** — the standard line/area chart of followers across the period (this is the same view you've had before).

entries.claim: The All Channels Posts card has its own view toggle.
entries.verbatim: Posts has its own toggle too — see **[Posts chart (All Channels)](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/using-insights-in-buffer-x4gLauQU5a#h-posts-chart-all-channels)** below.

entries.claim: Hovering over the Followers chart shows each channel's status for that day as a live number, an "As of [date]" carried-forward value, or "No data available."
entries.verbatim: Hover over the Followers chart to see each channel's status for that day: a number for a live reading, "As of [date]" for a carried-forward value from the channel's most recent data, or "No data available" if the channel doesn't have a reading yet.

entries.claim: For a date before a channel was connected, the Followers chart shows "No data available" for that channel.
entries.verbatim: If you choose a date range that starts before a channel is connected, hovering over a date prior to connecting the channel will show "No data available" for the affected channel.

entries.claim: The All Channels Posts chart has a Bar / Stacked Bar toggle.
entries.verbatim: Below the Followers table the Posts chart has its own **Bar / Stacked Bar** toggle:

entries.claim: The default Bar view is a horizontal ranked chart with one bar per channel, showing total posts over the selected date range from most to fewest.
entries.verbatim: - **Bar** (default) — a horizontal ranked chart, one bar per channel, showing total posts over the selected date range, sorted from most to fewest. Best for seeing at a glance which channel you posted to the most.

entries.claim: The Stacked Bar view displays vertical bars over time, with each day broken down by channel.
entries.verbatim: - **Stacked Bar** — vertical bars over time, with each day broken down by channel. Best for seeing when you posted most across the range and how that activity splits across channels.

entries.claim: Share as Post on the Posts table captures the view currently on screen, including the ranked Bar view.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** ***Share as Post*** on the Posts table captures whichever view is on screen, including the ranked Bar view.

entries.claim: Share as Post on the Followers table captures only the Over Time chart, even when By channel or Growth is displayed.
entries.verbatim: This differs from the Followers table above, where ***Share as Post*** only captures the Over Time chart even if you're viewing **By channel** or **Growth**.

entries.claim: The Compare dropdown can overlay data from an earlier period and offers five comparison options.
entries.verbatim: Use the **Compare** dropdown to overlay data from an earlier period. Five options are available:

entries.claim: Previous Period compares the selected date range with the same number of days immediately before it.
entries.verbatim: - **Previous Period** — the same number of days immediately before your current date range. Best for short-term trend checks (e.g. comparing this week to last week).

entries.claim: Same Period Last Month compares the selected date range with the equivalent calendar window one month earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Month** — the equivalent calendar window one month earlier. Best for monthly reviews where month-over-month progress matters more than seasonality.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Year compares the selected date range with the equivalent calendar window twelve months earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Year** — the equivalent calendar window twelve months earlier. Best for year-over-year reporting and tracking seasonal trends.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Week compares the selected date range with the equivalent calendar window one week earlier and is unavailable for ranges longer than 7 days.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Week** — the equivalent calendar window one week earlier. Best for short-range, week-over-week check-ins. (Unavailable when your selected date range is longer than 7 days.)

entries.claim: Custom period comparison is available only on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** (paid plans only) — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, cannot be selected.

entries.claim: A Custom comparison lets users select any historical start date and creates a comparison window equal in length to the current period.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** (paid plans only) — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, cannot be selected.

entries.claim: Custom comparisons cannot start on dates that overlap the current period or lie in the future.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** (paid plans only) — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, cannot be selected.

entries.claim: The chart can display the current period only as a solid line, the comparison only as a dashed line, or both periods together.
entries.verbatim: - **This Period** — shows only your current date range (solid line). - **Comparison** — shows only the comparison period (dashed line). - **Both** — overlays both periods on the same chart.

entries.claim: Hovering over a period-display toggle shows the exact date range it covers.
entries.verbatim: Hover over any toggle option to see a tooltip with the exact date range it covers, so you always know which window is which.

entries.claim: A comparison selection is saved in the URL and can be bookmarked or shared.
entries.verbatim: Your comparison choice is saved in the URL, so you can bookmark or share a specific view.

entries.claim: Channel and Tags filters can be combined to analyze a content category across selected channels.
entries.verbatim: 💡 **Tip:** Combine the channel filter with the Tags filter to see how a specific content category performed across your selected channels.

entries.claim: Takeaways provides AI-powered observations about recent content performance.
entries.verbatim: The Takeaways section provides AI-powered observations about your recent content performance.

entries.claim: Takeaways is not affected by the date-range selector and stays consistent while users explore different chart time windows.
entries.verbatim: Unlike the Summary and Metrics chart, Takeaways are not affected by the date range selector. They reflect a broader view of your content performance and stay consistent as you explore different time windows in the chart above.

entries.claim: All Channels Takeaways can show cross-channel highlights such as channels with replies waiting or posts with no comments.
entries.verbatim: On the **All Channels** page, Takeaways works a little differently. Alongside the same kinds of cards you'd see on a single channel, you'll also get cross-channel highlights — like which channels have replies waiting or which posts got no comments — plus a curated mix of standout takeaways pulled from your individual channels.

entries.claim: All Channels Takeaways includes a curated mix of standout takeaways from individual channels, linking to the corresponding single-channel Insights pages.
entries.verbatim: Alongside the same kinds of cards you'd see on a single channel, you'll also get cross-channel highlights — like which channels have replies waiting or which posts got no comments — plus a curated mix of standout takeaways pulled from your individual channels. Each of these links out to the full single-channel Insights page if you want to dig deeper.

entries.claim: Takeaways calculates engagement rate by pooling engagement and reach across posts before computing the rate, giving more weight to posts with greater reach.
entries.verbatim: **Note on engagement rate in Takeaways:** Takeaways calculates engagement rate by pooling engagement and reach across your posts first, then computing the rate — so posts seen by more people carry proportionally more weight than posts with only a handful of views.

entries.claim: The Takeaways engagement-rate calculation counts Instagram saves and LinkedIn comments as engagement.
entries.verbatim: This calculation also counts Instagram saves and LinkedIn comments as engagement.

entries.claim: Performance tips identify patterns including resonating formats, engagement-driving topics, and trends worth repeating.
entries.verbatim: - **Performance tips** highlight patterns in your content — things like which formats are resonating, what topics are driving engagement, and trends worth repeating.

entries.claim: Repost suggestions identify high-performing older posts and suggest republishing them.
entries.verbatim: - **Repost suggestions** identify your best-performing older posts and suggest republishing them to extend their reach.

entries.claim: A Start with AI card opens the post composer with the AI Assistant active and a performance-based prompt pre-filled.
entries.verbatim: - **Start with AI cards** are interactive. Click one to open the post composer with the AI Assistant panel already active and a prompt pre-filled based on what's been working for you.

entries.claim: Users can edit or run a Start with AI prompt and schedule the resulting post.
entries.verbatim: You can tweak the prompt or run it as-is, then schedule the resulting post like any other.

entries.claim: Draft reminders link to unpublished drafts and appear only when a channel has at least one draft.
entries.verbatim: - **Draft reminders** point you back to a draft you have not published yet. They only show when your channel has at least one draft.

entries.claim: When the newest draft is past its due date, Takeaways displays an overdue nudge.
entries.verbatim: If the newest draft is past its due date, you’ll see a nudge that it’s overdue.

entries.claim: The Review draft action opens the composer so the draft can be finished and published.
entries.verbatim: You can click ***Review draft*** to open the composer and finish publishing.

entries.claim: The repost takeaway appears only for channels with posts older than four weeks.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** The repost takeaway only appears for channels with posts older than four weeks and is not currently available for Bluesky or Mastodon channels.

entries.claim: The repost takeaway is not available for Bluesky or Mastodon channels.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** The repost takeaway only appears for channels with posts older than four weeks and is not currently available for Bluesky or Mastodon channels.

entries.claim: Each Takeaway card includes thumbs-up and thumbs-down feedback controls.
entries.verbatim: Each Takeaway card has a thumbs-up and thumbs-down button in its header.

entries.claim: Takeaway feedback remains highlighted and can be clicked again to remove the selection.
entries.verbatim: Your selection stays highlighted so you can see at a glance which cards you've already rated. Change your mind? You can click again to unselect your choice.

entries.claim: Insights supports Instagram Professional accounts, Facebook Pages, X/Twitter, LinkedIn Pages and Profiles, TikTok, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, YouTube, Mastodon, and Substack.
entries.verbatim: Insights is available for these channels: - Instagram (Professional accounts — Business or Creator) - Facebook Pages - X/Twitter - LinkedIn Pages and Profiles - TikTok - Pinterest - Threads - Bluesky - YouTube - Mastodon - Substack

entries.claim: Available Insights metrics vary by channel according to the data each social network exposes through its API.
entries.verbatim: **Good to Know:** The metrics available in Insights will vary depending on the channel. Each social network controls what data it makes accessible through its API, so you may see different metrics for different channels.

entries.claim: Insights numbers can differ slightly from native social-network analytics because platforms calculate and update data differently.
entries.verbatim: **The numbers may differ from your native analytics.** Small discrepancies between what you see in Buffer and what you see in Instagram, Facebook, or other native dashboards are completely normal. [Each platform calculates and updates data in its own way](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/why-your-data-in-buffer-insights-might-look-different-from-native-analytics-CryTKTdV0u).

entries.claim: Buffer offers help with missing expected historical data through hello@buffer.com.
entries.verbatim: If you're not seeing historical data you expected, reach out to our team at [hello@buffer.com](mailto:hello@buffer.com).

entries.claim: Instagram Personal accounts have restricted API access and limited Insights data; the full range of metrics requires a Professional Business or Creator account.
entries.verbatim: **Instagram Personal accounts have limited data.** To get the full range of metrics in Insights for Instagram, you'll want your account connected as a Professional (Business or Creator) account. Personal accounts have restricted API access.

entries.claim: Insights includes preset date ranges for Last 7 days, Last 30 days, and Month to date.
entries.verbatim: You can use the preset date ranges: - Last 7 days, - Last 30 days - Month to date - Last month (paid plans)

entries.claim: The Last month preset date range is available on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: - Last month (paid plans)

entries.claim: Custom Insights date ranges are available only on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: or set a custom range (paid plans only).

entries.claim: A post's engagement rate is based on its interactions relative to how many people saw it during the selected period.
entries.verbatim: Engagement rate is based on the interactions a post received (likes, comments, shares, etc.) relative to how many people saw it during the selected period.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profile posts, Buffer calculates engagement rate as (reactions + comments) / impressions because reliable reshare data is unavailable.
entries.verbatim: **Note for LinkedIn profiles:** Reshare data isn't available at a reliable level of accuracy for LinkedIn profile posts, so Buffer uses **(reactions + comments) / impressions** for the engagement rate on those posts.

entries.claim: LinkedIn Page posts use LinkedIn's reported engagement rate, which includes shares.
entries.verbatim: LinkedIn Page posts are unaffected — they use the engagement rate LinkedIn itself reports, which includes shares.

entries.claim: Instagram engagement rate is reported on the same 0–100 percentage scale as other networks.
entries.verbatim: **Note for Instagram posts:** Engagement rate is now reported on the same 0–100 percentage scale as every other network, so Instagram sorts and compares correctly alongside your other channels.

entries.claim: Exporting Insights as a PDF is available on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: Yes, on our paid plans. Click the **Export** button at the top of the page and choose **Export as PDF**.

entries.claim: PDF export configuration supports setting a report name, uploading a cover logo, and selecting included sections.
entries.verbatim: You'll first see a short configuration step where you can set a report name, upload a cover logo, and pick which sections to include.

entries.claim: PDF exports run in the background and generate a branded report.
entries.verbatim: Once you confirm, the export runs in the background and generates a branded report.

entries.claim: Single-channel PDF exports include a cover page, Summary metrics, Metrics-over-time charts, and a Performance per Post table.
entries.verbatim: Single-channel exports include a cover page, Summary metrics, Metrics-over-time charts, and a Performance per Post table.

entries.claim: All Channels PDF exports include an aggregated Summary, Top Posts by Reactions and Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and a detailed section for each connected channel.
entries.verbatim: All Channels exports include an aggregated Summary, Top Posts by Reactions and Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and a detailed section for each connected channel.

entries.claim: Free plans can download snapshot images using Download Snapshots.
entries.verbatim: Free plans can still download snapshot images for free using the ***Download Snapshots*** option in the same Export menu.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots packages every chart's Share-as-Post image, including all view variants, into one .ZIP file.
entries.verbatim: Click the ***Export*** button and choose ***Download Snapshots***. Buffer will package every chart's Share-as-Post image (all view variants included) into a single .ZIP for you.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots is available on every plan, including Free.
entries.verbatim: This option is available on every plan, including Free.

entries.claim: Users can save any combination of date range, comparison, channels, and tags as a named Insights view.
entries.verbatim: Yes — click the bookmark icon next to the filter controls to save any combination of date range, comparison, channels, and tags as a named view.

entries.claim: All preset date ranges and Custom ranges can be saved on both single-channel and All Channels pages.
entries.verbatim: All preset date ranges plus Custom are saveable, both on single-channel and All Channels pages.

entries.claim: Buffer's Advocacy team provides Insights support by email at hello@buffer.com.
entries.verbatim: Need help with Insights? Send us an email at [hello@buffer.com](mailto:hello@buffer.com) and our Advocacy team will be standing by to help.

entries.verbatim: - If your channel shows as **"Unavailable"** when you try to connect it ([like this](https://share.buffer.com/o0uwjnN0)), it's likely already connected to a different Buffer organization.
