entries.claim: Facebook personal profiles cannot be connected to Buffer.
entries.verbatim: - It's not possible to connect Facebook ***personal profiles*** to Buffer, as Meta prefers users not automate posting to these types of channels.

entries.claim: Buffer’s Free plan supports connections for up to three channels at once.
entries.verbatim: - While our Free plan supports connections for up to three channels at once, there is a *lifetime* channel connection limit of 8 channels per social network.

entries.claim: Buffer’s Free plan has a lifetime connection limit of 8 unique channels per social network, including channels that are no longer connected.
entries.verbatim: This means that, on the Free plan, we track the number of unique channels you've connected per social network, even if they're no longer connected (e.g. a user on the Free plan would only be able to connect 8 distinct TikTok accounts).

entries.claim: The lifetime channel connection limit does not apply to Buffer’s paid plans.
entries.verbatim: This lifetime limit does not apply to [our paid plans](http://buffer.com/pricing).

entries.claim: Users can reorder channels in Buffer’s channel menu by dragging them.
entries.verbatim: To reorder channels in the channel menu, click and drag a channel to your preferred position.

entries.claim: Newly connected channels appear newest first by default in Buffer’s channel list.
entries.verbatim: By default, new channels appear newest first in your channel list.

entries.claim: Buffer remembers a user’s preferred channel order after channels are rearranged.
entries.verbatim: Once you click and drag channels into your preferred order, Buffer remembers that order.

entries.claim: Team users, including Admins, may be able to see a channel under Manage Channels without having permission to access it in the Publishing tab.
entries.verbatim: - **For users on a team, including Admins:** If you can see a channel under ***Manage Channels*** but not in the ***Publishing*** tab, you may not have permission to access it.

entries.claim: A Buffer organization owner can update a team member’s channel access.
entries.verbatim: Ask your organization owner to update your access by following the steps in [Changing user permissions in your organization](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/changing-user-permissions-in-your-organization-yWbzm5BIgH).

entries.claim: Social channel access tokens can expire and require the channel to be reconnected.
entries.verbatim: - Social channel access tokens occasionally expire, requiring you to reconnect the channel.

entries.claim: Buffer lets users configure posting times for a channel queue.
entries.verbatim: - 💡 Once a channel is connected, set up your posting times so your queue can start filling.

entries.claim: Buffer allows multiple accounts from the same social network to be connected, such as two Instagram accounts or three TikTok accounts.
entries.verbatim: You can connect multiple accounts from the same social network, such as two Instagram accounts or three TikTok accounts.

entries.claim: Buffer connects the social account currently logged in to the user’s browser.
entries.verbatim: Buffer connects the account currently logged in to your browser, and no account picker appears during the connection process.

entries.claim: No account picker appears during Buffer’s channel connection process.
entries.verbatim: Buffer connects the account currently logged in to your browser, and no account picker appears during the connection process.

entries.claim: Using an incognito or private window can prevent Buffer from connecting to an account already signed in on the regular browser.
entries.verbatim: In the incognito window, log in to the account you want to connect to Buffer. This prevents Buffer from connecting to the account that is already signed in on your regular browser.

entries.claim: Facebook and LinkedIn Pages are authorized through a personal profile, after which Buffer shows the Pages that profile manages.
entries.verbatim: Facebook and LinkedIn work a little differently: you always authorize through your **personal profile**, and Buffer then shows the Pages you manage so you can pick the right one.

entries.claim: Authorizing Facebook or LinkedIn through a personal profile does not connect or post to that personal profile.
entries.verbatim: Signing in with your personal profile is normal and does **not** connect or post to that personal profile.

entries.claim: Connecting a Facebook Page to Buffer requires a Facebook profile with Full control of the Page.
entries.verbatim: - **Facebook Pages:** Sign in with a Facebook profile that has **Full control** of the Page.

entries.claim: Buffer may not find a Facebook Page unless Buffer is granted access to all Pages and groups under Facebook’s “Choose what you allow” settings.
entries.verbatim: Click **See all Pages** to expand the full list, then grant access to **all** Pages and groups. Otherwise, Buffer may not be able to find the Page you want to connect.

entries.claim: Not granting Buffer access to all Facebook Pages is the most common reason a Facebook Page does not appear during connection.
entries.verbatim: This is the most common reason a Facebook Page does not appear during connection.

entries.claim: Connecting a LinkedIn Page to Buffer requires Super Admin status; Content Admins and other roles cannot connect Pages.
entries.verbatim: - **LinkedIn Pages:** You must be a **Super Admin** of the LinkedIn Page. Sign in with your personal LinkedIn profile, then select a Page you’re a Super Admin of. Content Admins and other roles cannot connect Pages to Buffer.

entries.claim: Connecting a YouTube channel to Buffer requires the channel Owner role; a Manager cannot connect it.
entries.verbatim: - **YouTube:** You must be signed in as the channel **Owner**, not a Manager.

entries.claim: For a YouTube Brand Account channel, the owning Google account must be used to connect it to Buffer.
entries.verbatim: For Brand Account channels, sign in with the owning Google account.

entries.claim: Newly created YouTube channels may need to wait a day or two before they can be connected to Buffer.
entries.verbatim: Newly created YouTube channels may need to wait a day or two before they can be connected.

entries.claim: Connecting Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Substack, or X/Twitter requires being signed in to the exact account being connected.
entries.verbatim: - **Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Substack, and X/Twitter.** Be signed in to the exact account you want to connect before you start.

entries.claim: Users do not need to remain logged in to a connected social account for Buffer to post.
entries.verbatim: No. When you connect a channel, the social network gives Buffer an **access token**, which is like a secure key to access that account.

entries.claim: Buffer uses a social network access token to post on a user’s behalf while the login and permissions remain valid.
entries.verbatim: As long as your login and permissions stay valid, Buffer uses that token to post on your behalf, so you don't have to stay logged in to the social account in your browser.

entries.claim: Insights is a lightweight analytics view built into Buffer that shows follower growth, engagement, and impressions for one channel or a cross-channel overview.
entries.verbatim: It's a lightweight analytics view built right into Buffer — check in on a single channel's follower growth, engagement, and impressions, or get a cross-channel overview of how all your channels are performing, all without ever leaving your publishing dashboard.

entries.claim: Google Business Profiles are not supported in Insights due to API limitations.
entries.verbatim: **Note**: Google Business Profiles are not supported in Insights due to API limitations.

entries.claim: Insights can aggregate metrics from all channels into a bird's-eye view.
entries.verbatim: - All channel metrics aggregated for a birds-eye view, and

entries.claim: AI-powered Takeaways are available in both All Channels and individual channel views.
entries.verbatim: - AI-powered Takeaways, available on both the All Channels and individual channel views!

entries.claim: Key performance data is available inside Buffer without opening a separate analytics dashboard.
entries.verbatim: - **Stay in your workflow.** Key performance data lives right inside Buffer — no need to jump to a separate analytics dashboard.

entries.claim: Insights can show either a single channel's performance or all channels together in the All Channels view.
entries.verbatim: - **Check in on a single channel or all at once.** Drill into one channel's performance or zoom out to see how all your channels are doing from the All Channels view.

entries.claim: Insights can compare current numbers with the previous period, the same period last month, or the same period last year.
entries.verbatim: - **See what's working at a glance.** Compare your current numbers against the previous period, the same period last month, or the same period last year — handy for tracking seasonal trends.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post table ranks content by engagement rate.
entries.verbatim: - **Find your best posts fast.** The Performance per Post table ranks your content by engagement rate so you can spot what's resonating and do more of it.

entries.claim: The Metrics chart visualizes follower growth and other key statistics over time and can break growth down by channel.
entries.verbatim: - **Watch your audience grow.** The Metrics chart makes it easy to visualize follower growth and other key stats over time, or break growth down by channel to see where it came from.

entries.claim: Insights provides reach, impressions, and engagement-rate data.
entries.verbatim: - **Make smarter content decisions.** With reach, impressions, and engagement rate at your fingertips, you always have clear insights to guide your next steps.

entries.claim: “Start with AI” takeaways open the composer with an AI prompt prefilled from content that has been working.
entries.verbatim: - **Turn insights into posts in one click.** "Start with AI" takeaways open the composer with an AI prompt already filled in, based on what's been working for you.

entries.claim: Insights can be accessed as an overview across all channels or for a specific selected channel.
entries.verbatim: There are two ways to access Insights: **For All Channels -** Click ***Insights*** in the left sidebar of the web dashboard. Here, you'll see an overview of your Insights across all channels. **For a specific channel -** In the left sidebar, select the channel you'd like to view and then click ***Insights*** beneath the channel name.

entries.claim: Preview Mode provides a live sample Insights dashboard with real charts, sortable performance metrics, follower graphs, and top-post cards before a channel is connected.
entries.verbatim: **Haven't connected a channel yet, or just browsing as a guest?** Insights now shows a live sample dashboard — complete with real charts, sortable performance metrics, follower graphs, and top-post cards — so you can see exactly what Insights looks like in action before connecting a channel. Click **Preview Mode** to view data from Buffer’s own channels.

entries.claim: A channel's Insights dashboard defaults to the last 30 days.
entries.verbatim: You'll land on the Insights dashboard for that channel. It defaults to the **last 30 days**, but you can adjust the date range using the options at the top of the page.

entries.claim: Insights offers Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Month to date, Last month, and Custom date ranges, with Last month and Custom restricted to paid plans.
entries.verbatim: **Available date ranges:** - Last 7 days - Last 30 days - Month to date - Last month (paid plans only) - Custom (paid plans only)

entries.claim: The Custom date picker accepts natural-language searches for a specific month.
entries.verbatim: When you select **Custom**, you'll see a search box in the date picker that accepts natural-language queries. You can type: - **A specific month**, e.g. **April 2026** or **April**

entries.claim: The Custom date picker supports half-year shortcuts such as H1 2026, with H1 or H2 alone defaulting to the current year.
entries.verbatim: - **Half-year shortcuts,** e.g. H1 2026 (Jan 1 - June 30th, 2026). **H1** or **H2** defaults to the current year.

entries.claim: The Custom date picker supports relative ranges such as last 7 days, last 30 days, and last 365 days.
entries.verbatim: - **A relative range**, e.g. **last 7 days, last 30 days** or **last 365 days**

entries.claim: The Custom date picker supports month-to-month ranges such as April to May 2026.
entries.verbatim: - **A month-to-month range**, e.g. **April to May 2026, April 2026 - May 2026,** or **April - May 2026**

entries.claim: The Custom date picker displays suggested examples when it cannot understand a query.
entries.verbatim: If Buffer can't understand what you've typed, you'll see a small message below the search input suggesting examples. The message clears as soon as you keep editing your query or pick a supported format.

entries.claim: Custom and Last month date ranges are available on Essentials and Team plans, while Free includes Last 7 days, Last 30 days, and Month to date.
entries.verbatim: - The **Custom** date range and **Last month** is available on Essentials and Team plans. Free plan Insights includes Last 7 days, Last 30 days, and Month to date.

entries.claim: Any combination of date range and comparison can be saved as a named view and reopened with both settings restored.
entries.verbatim: - You can save any combination of date range and comparison as a named view — including the default **Last 30 days**, **Month to date**, **Last month**, **Last 7 days**, and **Custom**. Look for the bookmark icon next to the filter controls. Reopening the saved view restores both the date range and any comparison you had set.

entries.claim: Insights displays a “No Data Found” message when no posts or metrics are available for the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: **💡 No data for the selected period?** If there are no posts or no metrics available for your selected date range, Insights will show a "No Data Found" message in the chart.

entries.claim: Tags and Channels filters are available in All Channels, Instagram and Facebook can also be filtered by Post Type, and single-channel views can be filtered by Tags.
entries.verbatim: Both **Tags** and **Channels** filters are available in the **All Channels** view, and on **Instagram** and **Facebook** channels you can also filter by **Post Type**, making it easy to narrow down your Insights to just the posts or channels you care about. This makes it easy to track how a specific campaign, launch, or content theme is performing over time, without digging through individual post…

entries.claim: Insights can filter to one or more tags, search for tags, or select Untagged posts.
entries.verbatim: 3. Check one or more tags to filter your Insights to only posts that have those tags applied. You can also search for specific tags or select **Untagged** to see posts without any tags.

entries.claim: The All Channels channel filter controls every section of the Insights page, including the Metrics chart.
entries.verbatim: The channel filter at the top of the Insights page drives every section on the page, including the Metrics chart. There's no separate in-chart channel picker.

entries.claim: The All Channels filter supports selecting one or more connected channels, selecting all channels, and searching by channel name.
entries.verbatim: 3. Check one or more channels to narrow Insights down to just those channels. You can also use **Select all** to include everything, or search by channel name to find one quickly.

entries.claim: Tag and Channel filters can be combined to analyze a content category across a subset of channels.
entries.verbatim: **Tip:** Tags and Channel filters can be used together so you can see how a specific content category performed across a subset of your channels.

entries.claim: Facebook Groups, Instagram personal profiles, and Start Page are excluded from Insights data and exports.
entries.verbatim: **Note: Insights doesn't support every channel type.** Facebook Groups, Instagram personal profiles, and Start Page are greyed out in the channel filter and excluded from Insights data and exports.

entries.claim: A channel group containing only unsupported channels is disabled in Insights.
entries.verbatim: If a channel group contains only unsupported channels, the whole group is disabled too.

entries.claim: Instagram and Facebook single-channel Insights can be filtered by Post, Reel, or Story.
entries.verbatim: On the single-channel Insights page for Instagram and Facebook, you can filter your Insights by post type: Post, Reel, or Story.

entries.claim: Post Type filters can include one or more formats, while leaving all types unchecked includes every post type.
entries.verbatim: 3. Check one or more types to narrow your Insights to just those formats. Leave everything unchecked to include every post type.

entries.claim: A Post Type selection simultaneously filters the Top Posts table, Summary tiles, and Metrics chart and can be saved as a Saved View.
entries.verbatim: The Top Posts table, Summary tiles, and Metrics chart all narrow to the same selection. You can also save your filtered view as a Saved View.

entries.claim: Post Type filtering appears only on Instagram and Facebook single-channel views.
entries.verbatim: - It only appears on Instagram and Facebook single-channel views.

entries.claim: The Top Posts columns can change with the Post Type filter based on the metrics reported by the returned rows.
entries.verbatim: - The Top Posts column set can change with the filter. For example, filtering to Story drops any columns that Story posts don't report on (like engagement rate). This is expected: columns come from the metrics the returned rows report.

entries.claim: Followers, Reach, and Views charts cannot be narrowed by post type because they plot channel-level daily snapshots rather than posts.
entries.verbatim: - The Followers, Reach, and Views chart views can't be narrowed by post type. Those plot channel-level daily snapshots, not posts, so the filter doesn't apply. You'll see an inline notice naming any filter the chart can't apply.

entries.claim: CSV, Markdown, and PDF Insights exports are available on paid plans.
entries.verbatim: - **Exporting Insights data as a CSV, Markdown, or PDF file** is available on our paid plans.

entries.claim: Snapshot downloads are available on all plans, including Free.
entries.verbatim: - **Downloading snapshots** is available on all plans, including Free.

entries.claim: Members with view-only channel access can see Insights but cannot export them.
entries.verbatim: - Members with **view-only** access to a channel can see its Insights but cannot export.

entries.claim: When an All Channels selection includes channels with and without export permission, the export contains only channels the member may export.
entries.verbatim: On the All Channels page, if the selection mixes channels they can and cannot export, the file only includes the channels they have export access to.

entries.claim: Insights exports are available from single-channel and All Channels views and reflect the active date range, tag filters, and channel filters.
entries.verbatim: You can export your Insights data at any time, either from a single channel view or the All Channels view. The export reflects exactly what you're currently seeing on the page, including your active date range, tag filters, and channel filters.

entries.claim: PDF exports display up to 6 selected metric columns, using the first 6 in the chosen order and noting how many were included.
entries.verbatim: - PDF exports show up to 6 metric columns at once, so the layout stays clean and readable. If you've selected more than 6, you'll see the first 6 in your chosen order, plus a note showing how many of your selected columns made the cut.

entries.claim: CSV exports contain all selected metric columns in order, followed by a Statistics column containing everything else.
entries.verbatim: - CSV exports include all your chosen metric columns in order, followed by a Statistics column with everything else, so no data gets left out.

entries.claim: Insights exports preserve the active sort of performance and Top Posts tables.
entries.verbatim: - The active sort on the performance and Top Posts tables — for example, sorting All Channels by engagement rate will reorder the PDF's channel summary, the per-channel detail sections, and the top-25 channel cap to match

entries.claim: Insights exports preserve the columns selected in the single-channel Top Posts table and All Channels performance table.
entries.verbatim: - The columns you've kept in the column picker on the single-channel Top Posts table and the All Channels performance table.

entries.claim: A CSV export downloads as a .zip containing summary.csv, posts.csv, and timeseries.csv.
entries.verbatim: - **Export to CSV** — downloads a **.zip** file containing three separate CSV files: **summary.csv, posts.csv,** and **timeseries.csv**. Great for spreadsheets, client reports, and custom analysis.

entries.claim: A Markdown export downloads as one .md file containing all three Insights sections.
entries.verbatim: - **Export to Markdown** — downloads a single .md file with all three sections. Great for pasting into reports, docs, or AI tools.

entries.claim: PDF export supports a custom report name, an uploaded cover logo, and selection of included sections.
entries.verbatim: - **Export as PDF** — opens a short configuration step first, where you can set a custom report name, upload a cover logo, and choose which sections to include (see [Customizing your PDF export](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/using-insights-in-buffer-x4gLauQU5a#h-customizing-your-pdf-export) below). Buffer then generates a branded PDF report of your current Insights view.

entries.claim: An All Channels PDF export includes an aggregated Summary, Top 5 Posts by Reactions, Top 5 Posts by Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and detailed sections for each channel.
entries.verbatim: - For the All Channels view, the export includes an aggregated Summary, Top 5 Posts by Reactions, Top 5 Posts by Comments, a per-channel Performance table, and a detailed section for each channel with its own Summary metrics, charts, and top posts.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots exports all Insights charts as images.
entries.verbatim: - **Download Snapshots** — downloads all of your Insights charts as images for easy sharing

entries.claim: Insights export files generate in the background; smaller exports may download almost immediately, while larger exports may take a few minutes.
entries.verbatim: 5. The file will generate in the background. Smaller exports download almost immediately; larger ones (long date ranges or high post counts) may take a few minutes. A spinner will show while the file is being prepared so keep the tab open until the download starts.

entries.claim: A PDF report can use a custom title, or the organization name when the report name is left blank.
entries.verbatim: - **Report name**: a custom title shown in the PDF header. Leave it blank and Buffer will use your organization name instead.

entries.claim: A custom logo can replace Buffer branding on a PDF report cover, and Buffer saves the most recently uploaded logo for the next export.
entries.verbatim: - **Cover logo**: upload your own logo to replace the default Buffer branding on the report's cover. Buffer saves the last logo you upload, so you won't need to re-upload it on your next export.

entries.claim: Every PDF report section is included by default and can be individually unchecked.
entries.verbatim: - **Sections to include**: every section is on by default. Uncheck anything you don't want in the final PDF.

entries.claim: The export configuration step applies only to PDF exports; CSV and Markdown exports begin immediately without it.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** This configuration step only applies to PDF exports. CSV and Markdown exports run immediately, with no extra step.

entries.claim: Both export formats include data from all three Insights sections.
entries.verbatim: Both formats include data from all three Insights sections:

entries.claim: Insights exports include a Summary with each metric’s current value and percentage change versus the previous period.
entries.verbatim: - **Summary** — each metric's current value and its percentage change vs. the previous period.

entries.claim: Insights exports include one Performance per Post row per post with its ID, publication date and time, excerpt, type, URL, Buffer tags, and all available channel metrics.
entries.verbatim: - **Performance per Post** — one row per post, including Post ID, published date and time, a post excerpt, post type (image, reel, carousel, video, etc.), post URL, any Buffer tags applied, and all available metrics for that channel (impressions, reach, reactions, comments, shares, saves, engagement rate, and so on). Only metrics that exist for the channel are included.

entries.claim: Insights exports include daily followers, posts published, and post views for the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - **Metrics Over Time** — daily followers, posts published, and post views for the selected period.

entries.claim: Insights exports omit empty metric columns and include only metrics reported by the channel.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** Metrics included in the export vary by channel, just as they do in the Insights dashboard. You won't see empty columns — only the metrics your channel actually reports.

entries.claim: Each Insights export reflects the current filter state exactly.
entries.verbatim: **Tip:** If you want a different slice of your data, just update your filters and export again. Each export reflects the current state of your filters exactly.

entries.claim: The Summary compares channel performance during the selected date range with another chosen period.
entries.verbatim: The Summary section gives you a snapshot of how your channel performed during the selected date range, compared to another period of your choice.

entries.claim: The default Previous Period comparison uses the same number of days immediately before the selected range.
entries.verbatim: - **Previous Period** — the same number of days immediately before your selected range (default).

entries.claim: Same Period Last Week compares with the equivalent calendar window one week earlier and is unavailable for selected date ranges longer than 7 days.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Week** — the equivalent calendar window one week earlier. Best for short-range, week-over-week check-ins. (Unavailable when your selected date range is longer than 7 days.)

entries.claim: Same Period Last Month compares with the same calendar dates one month earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Month** — the same calendar dates one month back.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Year compares with the same calendar dates one year earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Year** — the same calendar dates one year back.

entries.claim: A Custom comparison can use any historical start date and creates a comparison window equal in length to the current period; overlapping and future dates cannot be selected.
entries.verbatim: - **Custom** — pick any historical start date and Buffer will use a comparison window the same length as your current period. Dates that would overlap your current period, or dates in the future, can't be selected.

entries.claim: Each Summary metric updates its percentage comparison indicator for the selected comparison period.
entries.verbatim: Each metric updates its comparison indicator (e.g. ↑ 28.6%) to reflect the period you've selected.

entries.claim: The Compare to dropdown is available only on single-channel Insights pages and does not appear in All Channels.
entries.verbatim: - The **Compare to** dropdown is currently available on single-channel Insights pages only. It does not appear on the All Channels view.

entries.claim: A bookmarked Insights view saves both its comparison choice and date range.
entries.verbatim: - Your comparison choice is now saved alongside the date range when you bookmark a view, so reopening a saved view restores both.

entries.claim: The Followers table shows current followers and the exact number gained or lost during the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Followers table sits right at the top, showing your current followers and exactly how many you've gained (or lost) over your selected date range.

entries.claim: Follower movement is displayed as a plain number such as +42 rather than a percentage.
entries.verbatim: We show that as a plain number, like +42, not a percentage, so you can see the real movement at a glance.

entries.claim: For networks that do not provide daily follower counts, Insights displays the most recent reading available in the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - Some networks only check in on your follower count every so often instead of daily. When that's the case, you'll see the most recent reading available for your selected period.

entries.claim: The Followers table is hidden when a channel does not report follower data.
entries.verbatim: - If a channel doesn't report follower data at all, the Followers table will be hidden.

entries.claim: The Posts metric counts posts published during the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Posts** — the number of posts published during the period

entries.claim: The Reactions metric totals likes and reactions received across all posts.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** — total likes/reactions received across all posts

entries.claim: The Comments metric totals comments received.
entries.verbatim: - **Comments** — total comments received

entries.claim: The Impressions metric totals the number of times posts were displayed.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** — total number of times your posts were displayed.

entries.claim: For Instagram, Impressions is labeled Views throughout Insights, including single-channel pages, the All Channels summary, and mixed-channel selections containing Instagram.
entries.verbatim: For Instagram, this metric is now labeled **Views** everywhere in Insights — on the single-channel page, the All Channels summary, and any mixed-channel selection that includes Instagram — matching what you see on Instagram's own Insights page.

entries.claim: The Shares metric totals shares.
entries.verbatim: - **Shares** — total shares

entries.claim: The Saves metric totals saves.
entries.verbatim: - **Saves** — total saves

entries.claim: The Follows metric counts new followers gained during the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Follows** — new followers gained during the period

entries.claim: The Reach metric counts unique accounts that saw the content.
entries.verbatim: - **Reach** — the number of unique accounts that saw your content

entries.claim: Engagement Rate is the percentage of people who engaged with posts among those who saw them.
entries.verbatim: - **Engagement Rate** — the percentage of people who engaged with your posts out of those who saw them

entries.claim: Summary metrics include comparison indicators such as ↑ 28.6%.
entries.verbatim: Each metric includes a comparison indicator (e.g. ↑ 28.6%) so you can see at a glance how things have changed.

entries.claim: Metric availability varies by channel according to the data each social network provides through its API.
entries.verbatim: - Not all metrics are available for every channel — it depends on what each social network shares through its API. For example, Saves may only appear for Instagram, and Reach may not be available for all networks.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profiles, Reactions counts only reactions on the post itself.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** count only the reactions on the post itself, matching what you'd see on LinkedIn.

entries.claim: For LinkedIn profiles, Comments includes nested replies beneath top-level comments.
entries.verbatim: - **Comments** include nested replies underneath top-level comments, since LinkedIn's own comment total works the same way.

entries.claim: The LinkedIn Reactions and Comments counting rules described for profiles do not apply to LinkedIn Pages because Pages use a different API without the same total breakdown.
entries.verbatim: - This applies to LinkedIn profile channels. LinkedIn Pages use a different LinkedIn API that doesn't break totals down the same way.

entries.claim: For Substack, Reactions counts likes on a Note and Comments counts replies.
entries.verbatim: - **Reactions** count likes on your Note, and **Comments** count replies.

entries.claim: For Substack, Restacks counts how many times a Note was restacked or reshared.
entries.verbatim: - **Restacks** count how many times someone restacked (reshared) your Note on Substack.

entries.claim: For Substack, Impressions counts every Note view and Reach counts unique viewers.
entries.verbatim: - **Impressions** count every time your Note was viewed, and **Reach** counts the unique people who viewed it.

entries.claim: For Substack, Shares counts clicks on a Note’s share link rather than restacks.
entries.verbatim: - **Shares** count clicks on your Note's share link, not restacks.

entries.claim: For Substack, Free Subscriptions and Paid Subscriptions count subscribers attributed by Substack to each Note.
entries.verbatim: - **Free Subscriptions** and **Paid Subscriptions** count the subscribers Substack attributes to each Note.

entries.claim: Engagement rate is unavailable for Substack because Substack does not provide the figures needed to calculate it.
entries.verbatim: - Engagement rate isn't available for Substack, because Substack doesn't share the numbers needed to calculate one.

entries.claim: Substack follower counts and publication-level statistics such as total subscribers and open rates are unavailable in Buffer and remain in the Substack dashboard.
entries.verbatim: - Follower counts and publication-level stats (like total subscribers or open rates) aren't available for Substack. Those stay in your Substack dashboard.

entries.claim: A single-channel Insights Summary can be turned into a ready-to-publish post.
entries.verbatim: On a single-channel Insights view, you can turn your Summary stats into a ready-to-publish post.

entries.claim: Share as Post generates a branded 1080×1080 image containing top statistics, the channel avatar, and Buffer branding.
entries.verbatim: 2. This will generate a branded 1080×1080 image showing your top stats (reach, likes, replies, shares, etc.) with your channel's avatar and Buffer branding.

entries.claim: Share as Post opens the Post Composer with the generated image attached, alt text set, and a short caption pre-filled.
entries.verbatim: 3. Open the Post Composer with that image attached, alt text set, and a short caption pre-filled.

entries.claim: A shared Summary post can be edited, assigned to channels, and scheduled or published like another post.
entries.verbatim: 4. Tweak the copy, choose which channels to post to, and schedule or publish like any other post.

entries.claim: Share Summary is limited to single-channel Insights and is absent from All Channels because no single default channel exists there.
entries.verbatim: - **Share Summary is only available on single-channel Insights.** It doesn't appear on the All Channels view because there's no single channel for the post to default to.

entries.claim: Share Summary images always use a 1080×1080 square layout accepted without further cropping by Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook.
entries.verbatim: - The image always uses a 1080×1080 square layout, which Instagram, X, LinkedIn, and Facebook all accept without further cropping.

entries.claim: A Share Summary card displays up to 4 available statistics from reach, likes, replies, and share-style metrics.
entries.verbatim: - Up to 4 stats are shown on the card, picked from what's available for your channel (reach, likes, replies, shares-style metrics).

entries.claim: Download Snapshots packages every chart’s Share-as-Post image into one ZIP without opening the composer.
entries.verbatim: 💡 **Tip:** Want to grab every chart's Share-as-Post image at once? Use ***Download Snapshots*** from the Export menu — it packages them all into a single ZIP without opening the composer. Available on every plan, including Free.

entries.claim: Download Snapshots is available on every plan, including Free.
entries.verbatim: Available on every plan, including Free.

entries.claim: The Performance per Post table breaks down each individual post’s results during the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Performance per Post table breaks down how each individual post did during the selected date range.

entries.claim: For each post, Performance per Post shows a thumbnail and content preview, engagement rate, reactions, comments, and views.
entries.verbatim: **For each post, you'll see:** - **Post** — a thumbnail and preview of the post content - **Eng. Rate** — the engagement rate for that post - **Reactions** — the number of likes/reactions for that post - **Comments** - **Views**

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Views counts how many times a Story was played.
entries.verbatim: - **Views**: how many times the Story was played.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Reach counts the unique accounts that saw the Story.
entries.verbatim: - **Reach**: the number of unique accounts that saw the Story.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, Replies counts replies sent to the Story.
entries.verbatim: - **Replies**: replies sent to the Story.

entries.claim: For Instagram Stories, engagement rate is calculated as Interactions divided by Reach.
entries.verbatim: - **Eng. Rate**: engagement rate (Interactions ÷ Reach).

entries.claim: Performance per Post columns can be rearranged using the column selector.
entries.verbatim: You can also rearrange the order of columns from the column selector, like this:

entries.claim: Performance per Post can be sorted by clicking a metric column header, with a second click switching between descending and ascending order.
entries.verbatim: Click any metric column header in the Performance per Post table to sort by that metric. Click again to switch between descending and ascending order.

entries.claim: Sortable Performance per Post metrics may include Eng. Rate, Reactions, Comments, Views, Impressions, Reach, Shares, Reposts, Clicks, Saves, Follows, Quotes, Total time watched, and Viewers.
entries.verbatim: Sortable metrics may include Eng. **Rate, Reactions, Comments, Views, Impressions, Reach, Shares, Reposts, Clicks, Saves, Follows, Quotes, Total time watched,** and **Viewers.**

entries.claim: Sortable columns vary by network and appear only where the channel reports the metric.
entries.verbatim: Sorting is per network. A column is only sortable where that channel actually reports the metric, so the sortable columns you see will vary by channel (for example, Facebook clicks are sortable on Facebook, and LinkedIn viewers and total time watched are sortable on LinkedIn).

entries.claim: Instagram Reels do not show a Follows column because Meta reports Follows only for Feed posts and Stories, not Reels.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** Some metrics also vary by post type. Instagram Reels, for example, don't show a Follows column, since Meta doesn't report Follows for Reels, only for Feed posts and Stories.

entries.claim: The Metrics section displays a line chart of a metric over the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: The Metrics section shows a line chart of a metric over your selected date range.

entries.claim: Date and tag filters do not affect the Metrics chart, which always displays the full year.
entries.verbatim: Note that date and tag filters do not apply to this chart — it always shows data for the full year regardless of the date range selected elsewhere in Insights.

entries.claim: A channel’s Metrics chart opens on Content Impact by default, overlaying posts and follower growth.
entries.verbatim: When you open a channel, the chart opens on **Content Impact** by default, layering your posts on top of your follower growth so you can see how the two track together.

entries.claim: The Metrics chart resets to Content Impact each time the user switches channels.
entries.verbatim: The default flips back to Content Impact each time you switch channels.

entries.claim: If a channel has no follower data, its Metrics chart opens on Posts instead of Content Impact.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** No follower data for a channel? The chart opens on **Posts** instead.

entries.claim: The Posts chart view shows how often content was published during the selected period.
entries.verbatim: - **Posts** — how often you published during the selected period.

entries.claim: The Content Impact chart view displays post volume alongside follower growth.
entries.verbatim: - **Content Impact** — your post volume alongside follower growth, side by side.

entries.claim: The Audience Growth chart view displays followers over time and net new followers gained.
entries.verbatim: - **Audience Growth** — followers over time, plus net new followers gained.

entries.claim: The Visibility chart view compares impressions—or Views for Instagram—with follower count.
entries.verbatim: - **Visibility** — impressions (or Views, for Instagram) compared against your follower count.

entries.claim: LinkedIn channels have a Follower Growth Rate view that benchmarks monthly follower growth against similar Buffer accounts.
entries.verbatim: - **Follower Growth Rate** *(LinkedIn channels only)* — your monthly follower growth rate benchmarked against similar Buffer accounts. See the callout below for details.

entries.claim: Paid plans can create a Custom Metric Set by selecting metrics to track together.
entries.verbatim: - **+ Custom Metric Set** (available on paid plans) — build your own view by selecting the metrics you want to track together.

entries.claim: Selecting a curated Metrics view button updates the chart automatically.
entries.verbatim: Selecting a button updates the chart automatically.

entries.claim: The metric dropdown can switch the chart to any individual metric available for the channel.
entries.verbatim: You can also use the **metric dropdown** (e.g. Followers) directly above the chart to switch to any individual metric available for your channel.

entries.claim: The Visibility tab appears only for networks reporting views data and is hidden for Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon.
entries.verbatim: - The **Visibility** tab (impressions, or Views for Instagram) is only shown for networks that report views data. It's hidden on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Mastodon channels — those networks only report follower counts at the channel level, so there's no views data to display.

entries.claim: The Follower Growth Rate benchmark is available only for LinkedIn channels.
entries.verbatim: - The **Follower Growth Rate benchmark** is available on LinkedIn channels only.

entries.claim: LinkedIn’s Follower Growth Rate benchmark plots monthly follower growth over time, compares it with the median of a similar-account cohort, and shows a percentile rank.
entries.verbatim: It plots your monthly follower growth rate over time and compares it against the median for a cohort of similar Buffer accounts, showing you a percentile rank so you can see where you stand relative to comparable pages.

entries.claim: The LinkedIn benchmark cohort matches accounts by channel type and approximate follower count.
entries.verbatim: - **What counts as a "similar account"?** The cohort is matched on two things: channel type (pages are compared to pages, profiles to profiles) and approximate follower count.

entries.claim: The LinkedIn benchmark cohort includes other LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer, not LinkedIn as a whole.
entries.verbatim: It's scoped to other LinkedIn channels connected to Buffer — not LinkedIn as a whole.

entries.claim: By default, the All Channels Metrics chart displays the first 5 channels.
entries.verbatim: By default, in the **All Channels view,** the Metrics chart shows your **first 5 channels**.

entries.claim: Applying the channel filter makes the All Channels Metrics chart display up to 10 selected channels at once.
entries.verbatim: Apply the channel filter at the top of the page, and the chart switches to your selected channels, drawing **up to 10** at a time.

entries.claim: When more channels exist than the chart can display, an inline notice reports how many are shown and suggests filtering by channel.
entries.verbatim: When more channels exist than the chart can show, you'll see an inline notice (*"Showing X of Y channels. Filter by channel to see a different set."*) in the section subheading.

entries.claim: A selected channel that does not report the displayed metric is excluded from the chart with an explanatory notice.
entries.verbatim: **Note:** Some metrics aren't available for every channel. If a channel you've selected doesn't report the metric you're viewing, for example Pinterest doesn't report followers, you'll see a notice like "Pinterest profiles don't report followers, so they are excluded from this chart," and that channel won't be drawn.

entries.claim: In All Channels, the Metrics area contains two stacked cards: Followers above Posts.
entries.verbatim: The All Channels Metrics area is split into two stacked cards — **Followers** on top and **Posts** below.

entries.claim: The All Channels Followers metric offers By channel, Growth, and Over time views.
entries.verbatim: In the **All Channels** view, the **Followers** metric has its own view toggle so you can choose how to look at follower counts:

entries.claim: The Followers By channel view is a ranked bar chart with one bar per channel, sorted by current followers.
entries.verbatim: - **By channel** — a ranked bar chart, one bar per channel, sorted by current followers.

entries.claim: In the Followers By channel view, the solid bar base represents the lower of the start or end value and the coloured segment represents the period’s change.
entries.verbatim: The solid base shows where you started or ended (whichever is lower), and the coloured segment on top shows the change for the period.

entries.claim: The Followers By channel bar label shows current followers and the change in brackets, such as 12,340 (+128).
entries.verbatim: The label at the top of the bar shows current followers and the change in brackets (e.g. "12,340 (+128)").

entries.claim: The Followers Growth view is a diverging bar chart of net change per channel, sorted with gains first.
entries.verbatim: - **Growth** — a diverging bar chart of net change per channel, sorted gains-first.

entries.claim: In the Followers Growth view, green bars indicate gains and red bars indicate losses.
entries.verbatim: Bars are coloured by direction — green for gains, red for losses — so you can spot at a glance which channels grew and which shrank.

entries.claim: The channel-colour legend is hidden in the Followers Growth view because colour represents direction.
entries.verbatim: The channel-colour legend isn't shown in this view because colour is being used to mean direction here.

entries.claim: The Followers Over time view is a line/area chart of followers across the period.
entries.verbatim: - **Over time** — the standard line/area chart of followers across the period (this is the same view you've had before).

entries.claim: The All Channels Posts card has its own view toggle.
entries.verbatim: Posts has its own toggle too — see **[Posts chart (All Channels)](https://support.buffer.com/en-us/articles/using-insights-in-buffer-x4gLauQU5a#h-posts-chart-all-channels)** below.

entries.claim: Hovering over the Followers chart shows each channel’s daily status as a live number, “As of [date]” for a carried-forward value, or “No data available” when there is no reading yet.
entries.verbatim: Hover over the Followers chart to see each channel's status for that day: a number for a live reading, "As of [date]" for a carried-forward value from the channel's most recent data, or "No data available" if the channel doesn't have a reading yet.

entries.claim: For dates before a channel was connected, the Followers chart shows “No data available” for that channel.
entries.verbatim: If you choose a date range that starts before a channel is connected, hovering over a date prior to connecting the channel will show "No data available" for the affected channel.

entries.claim: The All Channels Posts chart has Bar and Stacked Bar views.
entries.verbatim: Below the Followers table the Posts chart has its own **Bar / Stacked Bar** toggle:

entries.claim: The default Bar view ranks channels from most to fewest posts over the selected date range.
entries.verbatim: - **Bar** (default) — a horizontal ranked chart, one bar per channel, showing total posts over the selected date range, sorted from most to fewest. Best for seeing at a glance which channel you posted to the most.

entries.claim: The Stacked Bar view shows vertical bars over time with each day broken down by channel.
entries.verbatim: - **Stacked Bar** — vertical bars over time, with each day broken down by channel. Best for seeing when you posted most across the range and how that activity splits across channels.

entries.claim: Share as Post on the Posts table captures the view currently on screen, including the ranked Bar view.
entries.verbatim: **Good to know:** ***Share as Post*** on the Posts table captures whichever view is on screen, including the ranked Bar view.

entries.claim: Share as Post on the Followers table captures only the Over Time chart, even when By channel or Growth is displayed.
entries.verbatim: This differs from the Followers table above, where ***Share as Post*** only captures the Over Time chart even if you're viewing **By channel** or **Growth**.

entries.claim: The Compare dropdown can overlay data from an earlier period and offers five comparison options.
entries.verbatim: Use the **Compare** dropdown to overlay data from an earlier period. Five options are available:

entries.claim: Previous Period compares the current date range with the same number of days immediately preceding it.
entries.verbatim: - **Previous Period** — the same number of days immediately before your current date range. Best for short-term trend checks (e.g. comparing this week to last week).

entries.claim: Same Period Last Month compares with the equivalent calendar window one month earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Month** — the equivalent calendar window one month earlier. Best for monthly reviews where month-over-month progress matters more than seasonality.

entries.claim: Same Period Last Year compares with the equivalent calendar window twelve months earlier.
entries.verbatim: - **Same Period Last Year** — the equivalent calendar window twelve months earlier. Best for year-over-year reporting and tracking seasonal trends.

objections.objection: “The free plan already covers my needs, so there is no reason to pay yet.”
objections.answer: That is credible for a solo operator with three or fewer channels and a short queue. The paid case begins when they need more than 10 scheduled posts per channel, unlimited Insights history, advanced analytics, custom date ranges, exports, or paid-only publishing features. The evidence does not establish that every small user should upgrade.

objections.objection: “Per-channel pricing becomes expensive once every client has several social accounts.”
objections.answer: Buffer only charges for connected channels, permits channels to be removed as needs change, and discounts channels above 10. However, every connected channel is still billable on a paid plan, so the evidence reduces this concern but does not eliminate it for account-heavy agencies.

objections.objection: “I do not want to keep paying for a client's accounts after that client leaves.”
objections.answer: Channels can be removed as needs change, and Buffer's per-channel model means the agency is not locked into a permanent per-client package.

provenance.quote: They're never locked in indefinitely, and I don't want to continue paying for their channel when they're no longer in contract.

objections.objection: “Moving everything into another scheduler will take more effort than continuing with native platform tools.”
objections.answer: Buffer supports the major social channels in one workspace, offers a Free plan without a credit card, and provides 14-day paid trials. These points lower evaluation risk, but the supplied evidence does not quantify migration effort or show that existing drafts, history, settings, and workflows transfer cleanly.

objections.objection: “The analytics will not replace the native dashboards because metrics and capabilities differ by network.”
objections.answer: This objection is only partly answerable. Buffer provides single-channel and cross-channel views, post-level performance, comparisons, filters, and exports, but metric availability varies by API; Google Business Profiles and some channel types are excluded, and numbers can differ from native analytics.

objections.objection: “The queue is not flexible enough if my carefully timed posts cannot be moved.”
objections.answer: Next Available posts can be dragged, swapped, moved to the top, moved to the next open slot, or shuffled. Custom-scheduled posts are deliberately locked, and reordering requires selecting a specific channel, so the evidence confirms rather than fully resolves the limitation for date-sensitive calendars.

objections.objection: “My team needs approvals and permissions, but I do not want to pay for a collaboration tier.”
objections.answer: The Team plan includes unlimited team members, approval workflows, and custom channel access and permissions. There is no evidence of those controls on Free or Essentials, so buyers unwilling to pay the Team rate do not have a documented workaround.

objections.objection: “Scheduling posts is easy enough; I am not convinced another tool will materially save time or improve results.”
objections.answer: The strongest supplied proof is specific rather than universal: Kevin Indig reports saving two to three hours weekly on distribution, Josh Allan Dykstra schedules a month of posts in one day, and Foster Coffee Company reported 30% year-on-year follower growth while using Buffer. The evidence does not isolate Buffer as the sole cause of the growth result.

objections.objection: “Connecting client or company accounts will be fragile because I may not have the required permissions.”
objections.answer: Buffer documents the necessary roles: Full control for Facebook Pages, Super Admin for LinkedIn Pages, and Owner for YouTube channels. This explains how to avoid some failures, but it does not remove dependence on platform permissions, access tokens, or client cooperation.

objections.objection: “A tool that supports many networks may still leave gaps on the exact channels and account types I use.”
objections.answer: Buffer documents support by channel and capability, including where automatic publishing, notification publishing, analytics, advanced analytics, and engagement are unavailable. There is no complete answer when a required capability is absent for the buyer's account type; compatibility must be checked before purchase.
